Definition: properly, an absorbent, i.e. the bulrush (from its porosity); specifically the papyrus
BiblicalUsage: In the Old Testament, gômeʼ is the word for papyrus, a rush, a reed. In Exodus 2:3, the text says "she took for him an ark of bulrushes." In Job 8:11, the text says "Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?"
TheologicalSignificance: I take gômeʼ to mean that creation is God's handiwork, and it still speaks of Him to anyone willing to look. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
